what: Inside a long section (300vh by default), cards are stacked in one spot on a pinned stage, and in each interval of the section height divided by the card count, the next card rises straight from the bottom of the screen (100vh) and front (z 50) to cover (power1.out, scrub 1). From 35% of the covering interval, the previous card recedes to z −100 and the one before it to −200 into a 100vw perspective (viewpoint −50% above), so they look like strips layered, slightly shrinking upward. The large background text (bg) of the rising card floats up from 150px below, and the photo (media) grows from .8 → 1.

duration.One Card: Scroll by section height ÷ number of cards

options.z-in: Starting z (px) of the rising cards, default 50 — phone original is 15
options.z-back: z offset (px) the front card recedes by, the card in front of it doubles, default −100 — phone original is −20
options.at: Share of the cover range at which the previous card starts to recede, default .35 — phone original .5
options.rise: Distance the card starts lowered, default 100vh
options.from: Minimum window width to turn on (px), default 480 — narrower just stacks vertically
options.--fx-top: Height at which the stage sticks (css variable), default calc(50vh − 17.875rem) — subtract half the card height to center it
options.[data-fx-part=card]: Card — the first stays in place, the second onward stack over the first’s spot
options.[data-fx-part=bg]: (if present) big text behind the card — rises from below 150 and transparent

note: The original stacks cards on landscape screens (480 and up, landscape) and on phones (479 and below, z 15·−20·.5), and on tablet portrait it switches to cards rising from 60px below. That split is left to the caller, who swaps the options in with matchMedia
